sourceBindings.text: Two teaching soils at the same model pH5.2. Grain shapes are schematic, not measured texture or a count of acidity. Select a soil to inspect; no amount or predicted pH change is simulated.
Under otherwise comparable conditions, a sandy soil often has less buffering. The lime requirement is still tested, not calculated from particle appearance.
Clay and organic matter often increase reserve acidity and resistance to pH change. A suitable buffer/lime-requirement test is still needed.
Consider raising pH
Investigate possible lowering
Consider a soil-health input, not a pH cure
Insufficient evidence for that decision
Crop and suitable target
Representative pH result and named method
Appropriate buffer / lime-requirement test
Confirmed Mg or P status as relevant
Material effectiveness, quality and rate basis
Carbonates, irrigation water and site feasibility
Material maturity, salt/nutrient load and timing
Sentence starters, definitions and highlighted P/Al/Fe chart rows are available; no need to disclose a personal experience or invent a laboratory value.

units.delivery: Explain calmly and naturally to agricultural vocational learners in clear English. Read only the supplied connected passage with natural pauses. Preserve all negations, conditions, scene-safety restrictions and limits of training. Do not add medical advice, diagnoses, character voices, an introduction, music or an extra summary.

sourceBindings.text: Learner correctly states the direction of change, identifies calcium carbonate versus calcium-magnesium carbonate, describes sulfur's microbial oxidation and a crop/soil-specific reason to postpone a recommendation.
Pass with a qualified explanation, not a one-word product answer. A dose or immediate guaranteed pH change from pH alone does not pass.
Learner compares sand, clay/organic matter and calcareous soil using reserve acidity or buffering, and names the test, target, material effectiveness and field conditions needed for a site rate.
Pass when all decision inputs and limits are understood. No numeric application rate is scored without actual lab and site data.

Learner keeps A, B, C and soybean 5.2 as source model cases until verified; proposes measurement and diagnosis before conditional recommendations; explains when compost/manure/cover crops are useful but not automatic pH fixes.
Pass with evidence-based distinctions and an appropriate next check for each case. Symptoms or model key alone are insufficient.
